title: Viewport rendering blurry when using a window stretch mode
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in recent Godot versions: 4.7, 4.6, and 4.5 (I didn't go further back), both on Linux and MacOS (don't have a Windows machine to test it). ### System information Godot v4.7.1.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.5.2) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M3 Pro (Apple9) - Apple M3 Pro (12 threads) - 36.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description Hi folks, first bug report here so please let me know if I should include any additional information. Using SubViewportContainer with window scaling produces a blurry/pixelated output. My intent is to build a 3D split-screen display, and I can either: * Not define a window stretch mode, which gives me a sharp/native resolution display, but where UI controls like labels or buttons are not scaled. * Use a window stretch mode, which correctly scales UI controls, but causes the SubViewport output to be rendered at that scaled down resolution. With stretch: Without stretch: I have tried to set a "size 2d override" in the SubViewport, without success. ### Steps to reproduce Here is a basic scene to reproduce the issue: ``` - Node3d (root) - GridContainer (full rect) - SubViewportContainer (stretch: on) - SubViewport - Camera3D - DirectionalLight3D - MeshInstance3D (basic cube) ``` This setup is intended for a split screen display, where I can have 2, 3, or 4 SubViewportContainers. All works well until I go in the project settings and set `display/window/stretch/mode` to `canvas_height` and `aspect` to `keep_height`. I was also able to reproduce the same issue by downloading the [official split screen example](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/4.2-31d1c0c/viewport/dynamic_split_screen) and enabling stretch mode. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30453116/repro.zip)
